proved_mechanism: Installed Torch serialization._load creates a fresh local UnpicklerWrapper on each weights_only=False load. The find_class method uses super(), whose __class__ closure points back to the class; class dictionary/method/closure/class forms a cycle. CPython class MRO/dictionary can also be cyclic. Global gc.disable prevents these unreachable Python objects from being reclaimed.
not_proved: 400-load RSS is nearly flat; do not numerically extrapolate heap/RSS from this probe to1.25million scene loads
The observed original4.3GB training RSS increase may have multiple causes; no live GPU allocated measurement was available
GC0 success on CPU does not establish native-GPU/deserialization SIGSEGV safety
This probe simplified graph features and omitted Lightning/model forward; it is evidence for serialization/PyG object ownership, not full training memory behavior

source_lifecycle.finding: Dataset retains immutable raw filename lists and transform. get() returns each loaded dictionary, builder returns HeteroData. No append/list of historical scenes found in active path. Actual two native caches contain tokenized_agent/tokenized_map only.

BaseStorage._parent is weakref.ref. HeteroData→storage→parent therefore does not form a strong cycle. Collation keeps slice/inc tensor dictionaries for the current batch. DynamicInheritance also creates MetaResolver classes; no full-batch persistence seen in CPU probe.

Cached initial-state path returns fresh tensor dictionaries. Per-agent caches are added to local agent dictionary. self.token_traj_all in fallback token-library path replaces one latest-batch tensor rather than appending; current native initial_pos path avoids that fallback.

SMART_GAIL.training_step returns one loss; no historical training batch list. _log_train is step logging; training metric evaluators are inactive with limit_val_batches=0. Reference cache LRU and seen-set/histogram growth belong to evaluation, not this fit phase.

records is linear in updates but values are detached Python floats/dicts, not tensors. install() creates a model→bound capture method→closure(original bound model method)→model strong cycle, one per fit stage. Under globally disabled GC this can retain the model at teardown; not one cycle per training batch.

Trainer→loops→Trainer uses strong self.trainer; strategy holds model and LightningModule._trainer points back. Potential full stage/model retention after del trainer/model under disabled GC, especially repeated test Trainers; not measured by the no-Lightning probe.

generation_boundary_recommendation.pilot: Save real collector before any gc.collect monkey patch, keep automatic GC disabled, call that real collector(0) after completed training batch (outside torch.load and after optimizer/backward). Record actual collection return, gc counts, RSS and CUDA memory_allocated/memory_reserved separately. Keep parameters/data order/RNG/budget identical.
generation_boundary_recommendation.why: The observed local unpickler classes are newly allocated generation0 and unreachable once each load returns. A batch boundary avoids triggering collection in Torch rebuild. Live batch/model objects remain reachable; GC should not change physical inputs or optimizer state under normal object ownership.
generation_boundary_recommendation.limits: collect(0) does not collect old promoted unreachable objects. Surviving model/trainer/callback cycles can move to generation1; whole-stage teardown needs a separate policy or subprocess exit. gc.collect(1)/(2) traverses broader old framework/tensor objects and is a separate unvalidated risk, not automatically safe. torch.cuda.empty_cache only releases unused cached GPU blocks and cannot free live tensors held in cycles.
generation_boundary_recommendation.causality_rule: A successful pilot establishes observed bounded memory at that budget and timing only. It does not prove GC was the original SIGSEGV cause or validate multi-epoch exact-resume.

unpickler_owned_size_lower_bound.disclaimer: These are Python-owned shallow object sizes excluding shared globals/code/base classes and allocator overhead. Only a plausibility estimate if all such classes accumulate with disabled GC, never a measured RSS prediction.
